title: Pawns of Destiny: The King Changes Wings
summary: Walk the king across the board before approaching the checking rook from the side it cannot protect.

nodes.question: Why is Kd7 safe when an earlier central approach failed?
nodes.explanation: White is checked by Rc2. The king on c7 is high enough to protect a rook entry square on the eighth rank as it crosses to the other wing.

branches.title: Cross the board and chase the rook
commentary: Begin after ...Rc2+ in the five-piece later phase. Both a7 and h7 are ready to promote, and White must end the rook’s safe checking pattern.
Kd7 answers check and controls c8. Unlike an early central approach, the king now denies the rook its eighth-rank blockade.
Rd2+ follows the king with another file check.
Ke7 continues across the seventh rank, staying close enough to attack a rook trying to occupy the eighth rank.
Re2+ keeps checking rather than allowing either pawn to promote.
Kf7 keeps crossing toward the distant h-pawn. The black king remains stranded on b1.
Rf2+ repeats the file-checking pattern.
Kg6 turns downward on the opposite wing. The distant black king still cannot protect the rook’s checks near the h-file.
Rg2+ checks the king on the g-file.
Kh5 approaches from the edge rather than retreating toward the middle.
Rh2+ is another check, but the king is steadily closing the distance to the rook.
Kg4 approaches further while keeping both pawns ready to promote. Black’s checking rook has less room to stay away from the king.
Rg2+ is the illustrated final safe file check.
Kh3 attacks the rook on g2. A check on h2 could now be met by Kxh2, since Kb1 cannot protect that rook.
Ra2 stops the a-pawn from behind, but cannot stop h8 as well.
h8=Q promotes. White has ended the checking cycle and obtained a checked winning queen-versus-rook setup.
Rxa7 collects the remaining pawn, as shown in the last saved board. White still has an exactly checked queen-versus-rook win; this is not a claim that every such material balance always wins.
branches.explanation: Rxa7 collects the remaining pawn, as shown in the last saved board. White still has an exactly checked queen-versus-rook win; this is not a claim that every such material balance always wins.

branches.title: Hide behind the a-pawn
commentary: Compare the source’s idea of sheltering behind a7 instead of crossing the board.
Kb8 heads toward the a-pawn’s corner. It still preserves a win, but shelter alone will not finish the job.
Rb2+ checks along the b-file. White must choose its next square carefully.
Ka8 gives away the win by occupying its own promotion square. The exact position becomes drawn.
Rh2 stops the h-pawn. White has obtained shelter but not a useful promotion arrangement; this exact position is drawn.
branches.explanation: Rh2 stops the h-pawn. White has obtained shelter but not a useful promotion arrangement; this exact position is drawn.

branches.title: Approach the center one rank too low
commentary: This independently selected comparison tests why the king’s rank matters after ...Rc2+.
Kd6 gives away the win. The king is too far from c8 to punish the rook’s blockade.
Rc8 stops both a8 and h8 along the eighth rank. Unlike Kd7, Kd6 does not attack Rc8, and the exact position is drawn.

exercises.prompt: What changed to make the central crossing possible?
exercises.answer: The king has reached the seventh rank. Kd7 controls c8, preventing the rook from settling on the rank that stops both promotions.

exercises.prompt: Why approach the rook on the h-side?
exercises.answer: The black king on b1 helped protect checks near the a-side. On the other wing it cannot protect a rook on h2, so Kh3 ends the checking cycle.

startContext: Begin after ...Rc2+ at 101 seconds in the complete five-piece later phase. This is a different source clip from the earlier Pawns of Destiny study. The earlier checks and initial a7/h7 advances remain context. The final king crossing and corner shelter are reconstructed from saved images; Kd6 ...Rc8 is an independent comparison.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
